rationale: US Energy Logistics is Sixth Street's current manager-level name for the BP partnership platform. BP sold 49% of a controlled U.S. logistics affiliate in the first quarter of 2021 and retained 51% and control; 2023 reporting describes an expansion with the same 51%/49% split. Underlying pipelines and SPVs remain subordinate. The separate 2025 bpx Permian/Eagle Ford midstream transaction and an unlinked 2024 offshore sale are outside this canonical boundary.
recommendedChanges: Create one canonical US Energy Logistics company record.
Record BP as the 51% current controlling owner and Sixth Street as the 49% current non-controlling owner from the first-quarter 2021 close, using Lerado Investments, LLC where supported.
Treat the 2023 49% affiliate transaction as an expansion of the platform while preserving the exact affiliate and asset schedule as not publicly disclosed.
Keep Olympic Pipe Line, BP Midwest, Whiting-linked pipelines and other underlying assets/SPVs subordinate.
Do not merge the separate 2025 bpx Permian/Eagle Ford midstream transaction or the unlinked 2024 offshore transaction into this record.
unresolvedQuestions: Exact BP member and Sixth Street fund
Reconciliation of reported 2023 $400 million capital with BP's $517 million proceeds
Detailed governance terms and the identity of the unrelated 2024 offshore buyer
